name: Still Image Environment Composite
use_when: A still image should feel like a cinematic moving scene without fully animating every object.
The base image already implies environmental motion such as fire, sky, smoke, rain, light, or atmosphere.
A video needs a richer establishing shot, mood beat, thumbnail-to-motion moment, or visual bridge from a static asset.
avoid_when: The image is evidence, archival proof, or documentary material that should remain clearly still unless the treatment is disclosed.
No overlay matches the still image's perspective, scale, light direction, or tone.
The moving overlay would hide the subject, captions, product, UI, or proof.
The external overlay asset has unclear rights for the intended release.

timeline_pattern.pattern: base_still -> motivated_moving_overlay -> blend_or_mask -> resize_position -> local_light_match -> global_adjustment -> preview_edges -> export
timeline_pattern.layer_order_rule: Keep the still image as the base layer, then place environmental motion above it only where the still implies that motion exists.
timeline_pattern.asset_match_rule: Choose overlays by visual fit, not keyword alone: perspective, brightness, color temperature, edge shape, and motion direction must belong to the base image.
timeline_pattern.integration_rule: Use blend modes, masks, feathering, and local color correction before global filters so the scene does not look like stacked stickers.
timeline_pattern.rights_rule: Stock, library, generated, or downloaded overlays need source and license notes before publishable delivery.

motion.rule: Environmental motion should be subtle enough to make the still feel alive while preserving the original focal point.

keyframe_values.overlay_duration: Trim or loop overlays to cover the full still-image beat without visible start/end pops.
keyframe_values.mask_feather: Use enough feather that sky, smoke, light, or atmosphere edges disappear into the base image.
keyframe_values.position_scale: Resize and position the overlay against real objects in the still, then preview at delivery size.
keyframe_values.motion_density: Use one or two motivated moving regions before adding more environmental layers.

sound.rule: Add ambience only when the scene needs to feel present; fire, wind, rain, or room tone should be subtle and stay below dialogue or narration.

captions.rule: Captions should avoid the moving area if it carries the scene effect, and remain readable over both the static base and moving overlay.

color.rule: Unify the still and moving overlays with exposure, contrast, temperature, tint, and highlight checks after individual layers are aligned.

implementation.ffmpeg: Loop the still image for the target duration, overlay moving assets with blend=screen/lighten or alpha-preprocessed clips, use masked overlays where needed, then apply eq/curves/colorbalance as a final unifying pass.
implementation.remotion: Create a StillImageComposite component with baseImage, overlayVideos, blendMode, transform, mask, feather, durationFrames, and grade tokens.
implementation.blender: Use image/video planes or compositor inputs, mask moving regions with soft alpha, match color per layer, then add final compositor grade/glow.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Add the still image to the timeline, place matching moving clips above it, set black-background overlays to Screen, resize/position them, mask and feather partial replacements, then add an Adjustment layer or filter for the final look.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Place the still on V1, overlays on higher tracks, use Screen/Lighten blend or opacity masks with feather, nest complex composites, and finish with Lumetri adjustment layers.

common_mistakes: Choosing an overlay because the keyword matches while the perspective, brightness, or motion direction does not.
Leaving hard mask boundaries around sky or atmosphere replacements.
Adding too many moving regions so the still image becomes visually noisy.
Forgetting source/license notes for stock overlays.
Applying a global filter before fixing layer-specific mismatch.
qc: Can every moving overlay's purpose be named?
Does each overlay align with a plausible source or region in the still image?
Are mask edges invisible at delivery size?
Do the still image and overlays match enough in exposure, temperature, and contrast?
Do captions, faces, products, UI, and proof remain readable?
Are all external overlay assets manifest-ready for source and license?
